snippet.title: Mbosso - Buku Jero (Official Music Video)
snippet.description:
"Buku Jero" is an energetic street anthem that reflects the realities of everyday life through the lens of Tanzanian culture. Inspired by the familiar phrase "buku jero" (TSh 1,500), the song blends local slang, humor, and relatable experiences into a lively celebration of friendship, hustle, and resilience.

At its heart, the song is about people coming together and playing their part. It captures the contrast between everyday responsibilities and the freedom that comes with nightlife, where friends gather, have fun, and embrace life's unpredictable moments. While the atmosphere is playful and energetic, the lyrics also carry a deeper message: stay focused, rely on yourself, and remember that God is the ultimate guide through every step of life.

One of the song's most heartfelt moments is its tribute to mothers. Rather than asking for wealth, a mother prays for her child's life, protection, and future, reminding listeners that love, faith, and family are worth far more than money.

With its infectious chant, authentic street language, and clever cultural references, "Buku Jero" is more than just a party song. It is a snapshot of modern Tanzanian life celebrating loyalty, perseverance, and the idea that genuine happiness comes from the people around you, not the amount of money in your pocket.

About Darkoo:
Nigerian-born and London-raised, Darkoo’s love for music was nourished within her family home where the sounds of 9ice and D’banj, alongside Fela Kuti and Ebenezer Obey could be heard resonating around the house.  A self-confessed ‘Afro-head’, Nigerian superstars such as Wande Coal and Wizkid left a lasting impact on Darkoo, particularly after she moved to London around the age of seven. 

In 2019 Darkoo released her stand-out track, 'Gangsta' featuring fellow Londoner and rapper One Acen. Featuring her signature deep husky vocals, the track shot the teenager to fame, quickly becoming a TikTok favourite and was crowned the biggest Afrobeat Song of 2020 and earning her three MOBO nominations. 
Fast forward to 2024 and Darkoo’s viral hit ‘Favourite Girl’ earned her global critical acclaim, in addition to a two MOBO wins for song of the year and female artist of the year
